groups.title: Nominalization and the preterit-agentive foundation
groups.proposal: Treat structural nominalization as a typed conversion from an owner-issued VNC Result to an NNC Source. For the Lesson 35 preterit-agentive family, preserve the difference between its restricted-use preterit-predicate shape and its general-use compound shape, and select the shape from the resulting NNC state or continuation rather than from an example verbstem.
groups.writingJob: Capture an owner-issued preterit VNC Result with its complete typed Source and predicate structure, create a typed preterit-agentive nominalization Source, and derive restricted versus general use from the licensed NNC environment.
groups.readingJob: Show functional versus structural nominalization, agentive meaning, the eight-family inventory, restricted and general shapes, state and continuation distribution, and Canvas examples as proof rather than route admission.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses nominalization when it is the intended operation and chooses a genuinely intended agentive reading only where context leaves one open. The application preserves the source VNC and derives the available preterit-agentive shape from grammatical use.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the typed VNC Result-to-Source continuation and the canonical NNC owner. Do not add example-verbstem, copied-predicate, formula, restricted-shape, or general-shape controls.

groups.title: Absolutive preterit-agentive reanalysis
groups.proposal: Convert any compatible owner-issued preterit VNC predicate into the restricted-use nounstem of an absolutive-state preterit-agentive NNC. Preserve projective and reflexive object structure inside the nounstem, keep the preterit Ø as its final constituent, carry the VNC subject-number dyad into the NNC, remove any antecessive ō particle, and preserve class-conditioned perfective shape without limiting the route to listed stems.
groups.writingJob: Reanalyze the complete typed preterit predicate as a nounstem, preserve internal participants and the final preterit Ø, derive the absolutive NNC slots and class-conditioned c, qui, qu-eh, or other number realization, and retain passive-patientive, compound-source, affinity-plural, and preterit-as-present branches when their typed facts license them.
groups.readingJob: Show the source VNC and resulting NNC structures side by side, predicate-to-nounstem rank change, retained objects and reflexives, final preterit Ø, removed ō, verbstem class and shape evidence, affinity plural, passive patientive, compound Source, and non-authorizing examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the nominalization and any genuinely optional affinity plural or agentive-versus-patientive interpretation licensed by the typed voice and context. The application derives reanalysis, class shape, internal placement, final Ø, number realization, and particle removal.
groups.controlPolicy: Accept every compatible typed VNC Result regardless of example identity. Do not add manual predicate copying, Ø placement, ō deletion, class-ending, internal-object, reflexive-position, or example-stem controls.

groups.title: Number, animacy, and object activation
groups.proposal: Derive the singular or common number position of absolutive preterit-agentive NNCs from the typed source and lexical analysis: qui-Ø, silent ⎕-Ø, or a genuinely licensed alternative. Preserve the Canvas tendency associating silent number with nonanimate reference without turning it into a universal rule. Where Canvas licenses it, allow an internal nonspecific object to activate as a specific projective object for supplementation, producing the typed verbal-plus-nominal hybrid.
groups.writingJob: Compute number-dyad availability from the typed preterit source and lexical facts, derive animate or nonanimate interpretations without forcing the stated tendency, and use the canonical participant and supplementation owners for licensed object activation while preserving all internal Source structure.
groups.readingJob: Show qui versus silent number evidence, whether the choice is fixed or open, animate and nonanimate interpretations, lexicalized contrasts, the non-universal tendency, activated-object origin and destination, supplementary-object need, hybrid structure, and homonym distinctions.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses qui versus silent number only when both are genuinely licensed and meaningful; any animate versus nonanimate interpretation remains a choice only when context does not decide it. The application derives fixed distributions and validates any licensed object activation from typed participant facts.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer a universal animate rule from a tendency, do not whitelist the examples, and do not let a user freely move objects. Expose only attested lexical alternatives and a real participant or interpretation choice.

groups.title: The general-use preterit-agentive cā stem
groups.proposal: Build the general-use preterit-agentive nounstem by demoting the restricted preterit predicate to an embed and adding the fixed Subclass 1-A matrix cā. Preserve the final preterit Ø immediately before cā, change an embedded reflexive to its shuntline ne shape, and reserve the rare archaic quē matrix for its explicitly typed lexical context.
groups.writingJob: Transform an owner-issued restricted agentive Source into the typed predicate-Ø-cā general-use compound and make it available to possessive state, adverbial use, and compatible NNC or VNC compounds.
groups.readingJob: Show embed and cā matrix, final Ø adjacency, reflexive shuntline realization, general-use distribution, cā class history, and the rare quē lexical formation.
groups.decisionSplit: The application derives cā general use automatically from the required environment. A quē choice appears only when an archaic lexical record explicitly licenses it.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add routine cā, Ø placement, reflexive-shape, or rank controls. Keep quē restricted and typed rather than productive by example analogy.

groups.title: Possessive-state preterit-agentive NNCs
groups.proposal: Inflect the general-use cā compound as a Subclass 1-A tl nounstem in possessive state, deriving uh-Ø for singular and hu-ān for plural while preserving subject, possessor, reflexive, projective object, patientive, yō irregularity, ya-uh lexical behavior, and licensed secondary possession.
groups.writingJob: Pass the typed general-use agentive Source through the canonical possessive NNC owner, derive the correct number dyad and participant carriers, and preserve only explicitly licensed irregular or recursive formations.
groups.readingJob: Show subject and possessor, cā general-use stem, uh or huān number, internal participants, irregular cā-yō, patientive counterpart, ya-uh and tē-to-ti lexical evidence, and secondary possession.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses intended possession and genuine possessor or participant reference. The application derives cā, state, person carriers, number dyad, and automatic boundary changes; lexical irregularities require typed records.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add uh-versus-huān, cā insertion, pronoun-repair, or example controls. Do not generalize ya-uh or cā-yō exceptions.

groups.title: Agentive embeds in NNCs and VNCs
groups.proposal: Use the general-use preterit-agentive Source productively as an embed in compatible ordinary NNC, VNC, and affective matrices. Preserve cā, typed compound boundaries, participant structure, and the narrow licensed hybrid in which an internal object activates for a supplementary object.
groups.writingJob: Recapture the owner-issued general-use agentive Result, pass it to canonical compound and affective owners, and validate any hybrid object activation through typed participant and supplementation facts.
groups.readingJob: Show agentive embed Source, cā boundary, target matrix, NNC or VNC Result kind, affective meaning and number, participant retention, hybrid activation, supplementary object, and examples as proof only.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended compatible compound or affective operation and any genuine affective meaning. Placement, cā form, matrix result, and object activation consequences are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not whitelist target matrices by examples or accept copied agentive strings. Reuse canonical compound, affective, participant, and supplementation owners.

groups.title: Old-woman agentive and nominal families
groups.proposal: Preserve the typed ilama-ti verbal derivation, its class-conditioned perfective t or h shapes, absolutive agentive, cā general-use, possessive, affective, yō, and ordinary ilama nounstem branches without collapsing their distinct Sources.
groups.writingJob: Build each licensed old-woman formation from the correct typed verbal or nominal Source and reuse the canonical agentive, possessive, affective, and compound owners.
groups.readingJob: Show verbal versus nominal Source, perfective t or h, number, cā general use, possessive and affective forms, yō meaning, variant ilan nounstem, and distinct lexical compounds.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended verbal-agentive or ordinary nominal meaning and compatible operation. Class shape and downstream formation are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not treat surface ilama similarity as Source identity and do not generalize lexical compound meanings.

groups.title: Old-man agentive versus drum nounstem
groups.proposal: Keep the huē-huē-ti preterit-agentive family distinct from the reduplicative huē-huē nounstem meaning old man or upright drum. Preserve vowel quantity, glottalization, final t or h, n-stem variant, Source history, and double-nucleus versus single-compound structure.
groups.writingJob: Select the typed verbal or nominal Source analysis, derive only its licensed agentive, possessive, affective, yō, embed, matrix, or compound forms, and maintain exact internal boundaries.
groups.readingJob: Show verbal versus nominal Source, vowel length and glottal evidence, preterit Ø, cā, n variant, drum and old-man meanings, lexical embed restrictions, and double- versus single-nucleus contrast.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended Source analysis and lexical meaning when phonology alone leaves ambiguity. The application derives the compatible structure and blocks cross-analysis continuation.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not merge homophonous shapes or let example compounds authorize productive routes. Preserve exact quantity and boundary evidence.

groups.title: Ownerhood with the ē matrix
groups.proposal: Build preterit-agentive ownerhood from a typed general-use incorporated nounstem plus the fixed verbal matrix ē when the noun class, subclass, final environment, and any lexical exception license it. Preserve preterit-only restriction, connective-t continuation, final Ø, boundary deletions, h-to-y behavior, and optional ē versus huā only where Canvas leaves a real alternative.
groups.writingJob: Select ē from typed noun-class and boundary facts, build the incorporated-object preterit predicate, nominalize it through the agentive owner, and preserve licensed recursive general-use continuation.
groups.readingJob: Show incorporated Source class and shape, ē matrix, preterit restriction, final Ø, boundary changes, optional matrix alternative, general-use cā continuation, lexical exceptions, and non-authorizing examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses ē versus huā only where both are genuinely licensed by the typed Source. Class-conditioned selection, deletion, assimilation, and nominalization are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Canvas examples prove class and boundary rules; they never form an ownerhood stem whitelist. Keep true lexical exceptions typed.

groups.title: Ownerhood with the huā matrix
groups.proposal: Build ownerhood with the fixed huā matrix for typed tl, tli, in, zero, general-use agentive, and recursive Sources where class and final-edge rules license it. Derive w assimilation, permitted ē alternatives, and all recursive cā boundaries without using the listed nouns as admission gates.
groups.writingJob: Select and realize huā from typed Source class, subclass, final edge, and lexical facts, then nominalize the preterit predicate and preserve recursive ownerhood structure.
groups.readingJob: Show incorporated Source, huā matrix, class reason, w assimilation, ē alternative, final Ø, general-use cā, recursion, and lexical exceptions.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a matrix only for a genuine typed alternative. The application derives the default matrix, assimilation, preterit form, nominalization, and recursive hierarchy.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not whitelist nounstems or create manual w-deletion, cā, Ø, or recursion controls.

groups.title: Abundant ownerhood with yo-ā
groups.proposal: Use the fixed Class C yo-ā ownerhood matrix for abundant, characteristic, or throughout possession, restricted to preterit predicate use, connective-t continuation, and preterit-agentive nominalization. Derive y assimilation from the typed boundary and allow recursive agentive incorporation.
groups.writingJob: Combine an open typed incorporated nounstem with yo-ā, derive its preterit predicate and assimilation, and pass it into connective-t or preterit-agentive owners with recursive Source preservation.
groups.readingJob: Show ordinary versus abundant ownerhood meaning, yo-ā matrix, preterit restriction, connective-t branch, final Ø, assimilation, general-use cā, recursion, and examples as evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses ordinary versus abundant ownerhood meaning. The application derives matrix, boundary assimilation, preterit shape, nominalization, and continuation.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not reduce yo-ā to an untyped suffix, whitelist incorporated nouns, or add manual assimilation controls.

groups.title: Ownerhood analysis and translation
groups.proposal: Apply ordinary and abundant ownerhood productively in absolutive, possessive, recursive, supplemented, and affective structures. Preserve subject animacy and lexical meaning distinctions without treating English have, covered with, married, famous, or similar translations as separate routes.
groups.writingJob: Run typed ē, huā, and yo-ā ownerhood Sources through canonical NNC, supplementation, recursion, possession, and affective owners while keeping their Source distinctions intact.
groups.readingJob: Show ownerhood matrix, ordinary or abundant meaning, subject animacy, state, recursion, supplementation, affective continuation, compositional meaning, idiomatic translation, and lexical distinctions.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses intended ownerhood meaning, subject interpretation, and compatible continuation only where genuinely open. The application derives structure and keeps translation separate from route authority.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not create English-translation routes or example-based lexical gates. Preserve true lexicalized readings as typed facts.

groups.title: Preterit-agentive embeds in VNCs
groups.proposal: Use owner-issued general-use preterit-agentive Sources as incorporated objects, manner adverbs, and complements in compatible VNC matrices. Derive subject- versus object-oriented manner, mainline versus shuntline reflexive shape from matrix valence, preserve lexicalized reflexive exceptions, and license object activation only in the narrow Canvas hybrid.
groups.writingJob: Pass the typed agentive Source to canonical VNC compound owners, select role and orientation when genuinely intended, derive reflexive line from matrix valence, and validate lexicalized exceptions and activated objects through typed records.
groups.readingJob: Show agentive embed, VNC matrix and valence, object/adverb/complement role, orientation, reflexive line and agreement, lexicalization, optional ye matrix, activated object, negation scope, and resulting valence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended compatible embed role, manner orientation, complement relation, and only a genuine ye alternative. The application derives reflexive line, agreement, valence consequences, and narrow activation.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not use the listed matrices as a route whitelist. Require typed matrix compatibility and owner-issued agentive Results; do not permit free object escape.

groups.title: Vocative realization of preterit-agentive NNCs
groups.proposal: Attach the vocative particle é to an owner-issued preterit-agentive NNC and derive qu spelling, supportive-i loss, stem-final k realization, and optional intervocalic h-to-y from the exact number dyad and boundary environment.
groups.writingJob: Combine the typed agentive NNC Result with the canonical vocative particle and derive its boundary realization without confusing singular vocative que with plural qu-eh.
groups.readingJob: Show source class and number dyad, vocative boundary, qu spelling, supportive-i deletion, stem-final k, optional h or y, singular versus plural analysis, and traditional spelling ambiguity.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses vocative use and only a genuinely licensed h-versus-y variant. The application derives all other boundary spelling and number distinctions.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add manual qu spelling, supportive-i deletion, or singular/plural repair controls.

groups.title: Double-nucleus ownerhood embeds
groups.proposal: Allow the fixed ownerhood matrices ē, huā, and yo-ā to incorporate an owner-issued, lexicalized double-nucleus NNC structure. Preserve fixed clause order, supplementation relation, internal person positions, principal number deletion, matrix orientation, and the complete canonical component Results.
groups.writingJob: Capture the licensed double-nucleus structure through canonical clause composition, downgrade it as one typed incorporated object, and apply the ownerhood matrix without letting the outer subject overwrite protected internal person structure.
groups.readingJob: Show both source NNC Results, fixed order and lexical meaning, supplementation relation, downgraded principal and possessor roles, retained internal person positions, deleted principal number, ownerhood matrix, and outer-subject independence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a double-nucleus ownerhood use only when a typed lexicalized unit licenses it. The application derives downgrade, protected internal structure, matrix orientation, and outer agreement.
groups.controlPolicy: Require owner-issued component Results and a typed lexicalized double-nucleus record. Do not accept strings, formulas, arbitrary clause pairs, manual deletion, or manual internal-person protection.
